the morphological changes in the brain in infant cerebral palsy are characterized by a combination of the following features: the dysontogenetic changes of the brain structures; disturbances of the cerebral vascularization; focal inflammation of the central nervous system, predominantly in the regions of lateral ventricles; the focal dystrophic changes of structural elements of the central nervous systems; the compensatory and regenerative changes in the central nervous system.
the morphological basis for ICP is a combination of dysontogenetic, cerebrovascular, dystrophic, and inflammatory changes in the brain.

the development of ICP is a multifactorial process, which is characterized by the combination of the following factors: dysontogenesis of the brain structures, cerebrovascular disturbance, focal inflammation and focal dystrophy of the brain structures.
